title: ACGS / gove-zone compliance control mapping
disclaimer: Self-assessment mapping, not a certification, attestation, or audit result. gove-zone is alpha / local-proof software. A mapping row means the receipt membrane produces evidence toward the requirement at the executor boundary; it does not mean adopting gove-zone makes a system compliant. Compliance is a property of an organization and its full control set. See docs/COMPLIANCE_CROSSWALK.md and docs/CLAIMS.md rows 27-33.
status_rollup_rule: When a requirement maps to a mix of default-on and opt-in controls, status reflects whether the default-on subset alone delivers the core of the requirement; opt-in components are disclosed in the limitation field. If the requirement's core depends on an opt-in control (or on operator-supplied strength, e.g. identity), the row is downgraded to partial.

status_vocabulary.implemented: Control is on by default and covered by tests in this repository.
status_vocabulary.opt-in: Control exists and is tested but must be explicitly enabled by the integrator.
status_vocabulary.partial: Control contributes evidence toward the requirement but does not satisfy it alone.
status_vocabulary.operator-owned: Requirement is an organizational/operator responsibility; ACGS only supplies supporting evidence.
status_vocabulary.gap: Requirement is in scope for ACGS but not yet covered.
status_vocabulary.not-applicable: Requirement targets system types or obligations outside ACGS scope.

RECEIPT-REQUIRED.enforces: No receipt, no execution at the governed executor boundary

ACTOR-ANCHOR.enforces: Gate caller identity must equal receipt.actor; validator != caller

HASH-INTEGRITY.enforces: Recompute receipt_hash; any field edit rejected (anti-downgrade)

SIG-VERIFY.enforces: A receipt claiming a signature must verify (Ed25519)

DECISION-GATE.enforces: DENY / ESCALATE / unknown decisions cannot authorize execution

ARG-BIND.enforces: Executed arguments must hash to argument_hash or equal the approved transformed set

POLICY-TENANT-BIND.enforces: Policy bundle/hash, tenant, boundary, action, audit-event hash must match expected

MACI-VALIDATOR-SEP.enforces: Proposer != validator at issuance and at the gate

POLICY-BEFORE-EXEC.enforces: Policy evaluated and appended to audit before any tool runs

FAILCLOSED.enforces: Policy exception/timeout -> synthesized DENY; audit append failure -> AuditError

AUDIT-HASHCHAIN.enforces: Append-only JSONL, previous_hash -> event_hash chain, flock+fsync, verify_chain re-walk

EXPIRY.enforces: expires_at enforced when set; unparseable timestamps reject

ANTI-REPLAY.enforces: Single-use receipts via persistent consumption ledger keyed on audit_event_hash

REPLAY-VERIFY.enforces: Re-derive decision by re-running policy; side-store args cross-checked against chain argument_hash

ESCALATE-HUMAN.enforces: ESCALATE decisions route to human authority and are not executable until resolved

eu_ai_act.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) — logging requirements
eu_ai_act.scope_note: Mapped against the record-keeping obligations for high-risk AI systems. ACGS is a governance component, not itself a classified high-risk AI system; these rows describe the logging evidence ACGS supplies to a provider/deployer who carries the obligation.

requirements.requirement: Art. 12(1) — high-risk AI systems shall technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system
requirements.limitation: Automatic recording covers governed side effects only; calls not routed through the executor gate are not logged.

requirements.requirement: Art. 12(2)(a) — logging shall enable identification of situations that may result in the AI system presenting a risk or in a substantial modification
requirements.limitation: DENY/ESCALATE events are recorded with full context; interpreting which events constitute 'risk situations' is operator analysis on top of the log.

requirements.requirement: Art. 12(2)(b) — logging shall facilitate post-market monitoring referred to in Art. 72
requirements.verification_method: uv run --package gove-zone python -m pytest packages/gove-zone/tests/test_replay.py --import-mode=importlib -q
requirements.limitation: Hash-chained decisions are replayable evidence inputs to a post-market monitoring plan; the plan itself is a provider obligation.

requirements.requirement: Art. 12(2)(c) — logging shall facilitate monitoring of the operation of the high-risk AI system by deployers (Art. 26(5))
requirements.verification_method: uv run --package gove-zone python -m pytest packages/gove-zone/tests/test_cli.py --import-mode=importlib -q
requirements.limitation: CLI verify/proofpack surfaces chain integrity locally; continuous operational monitoring tooling is deployer-owned.

requirements.requirement: Art. 12(3) — biometric-specific minimum logging (period of each use, reference database, input data leading to a match, identity of verifying persons)
requirements.limitation: ACGS is not a remote biometric identification system; generic receipts do record actor, timestamp, and bound arguments if an integrator governs such a system.

requirements.requirement: Art. 19 — providers shall keep automatically generated logs under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, at least six months
requirements.limitation: Audit is local JSONL, tamper-evident not tamper-proof; retention period, off-host/WORM durability, and custody are operator responsibilities.

requirements.requirement: Art. 26(6) — deployers shall keep logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, at least six months
requirements.limitation: Same as Art. 19: ACGS produces the log artifact; retention/storage lifecycle is the deployer's.

nist_ai_rmf.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
nist_ai_rmf.scope_note: Function-level mapping consistent with docs/COMPLIANCE_CROSSWALK.md; a row means 'contributes evidence toward the outcome', not full subcategory satisfaction.

requirements.requirement: GOVERN 1 — policies, processes, and procedures to manage AI risk are in place and enforced
requirements.limitation: Runtime policy bundles are not an organizational AI risk management program; they are its enforcement point.

requirements.requirement: GOVERN 2 — accountability structures and separation of duties for AI actors
requirements.limitation: Actor identity is opaque strings bound into receipts; authentication and IAM are external.

requirements.requirement: GOVERN 1.5 / 4.1 — accountability, transparency, and documentation of AI system decisions
requirements.limitation: Every governed side effect emits a tamper-evident Decision Receipt; ungoverned paths emit nothing.

requirements.requirement: MAP 1 / MAP 5 — context establishment and per-action risk framing
requirements.limitation: Decisions are categorized ALLOW/DENY/ESCALATE/TRANSFORM with bound arguments; upstream risk assessment quality is integrator-owned.

requirements.requirement: MEASURE 2 / MEASURE 4 — evaluate trustworthiness characteristics and track them over time
requirements.verification_method: uv run --package gove-zone python -m pytest packages/gove-zone/tests/test_replay.py packages/gove-zone/tests/test_replay_store.py --import-mode=importlib -q
requirements.limitation: Audit-only replay is policy-version-only; strong replay of full arguments requires the opt-in side store.

requirements.requirement: MANAGE 2 / MANAGE 4 — risk treatment, fail-safe behavior, monitoring and response
requirements.limitation: Fail-closed and decision gating are default-on; expiry is an opt-in field and anti-replay is an opt-in ledger.

iso_42001.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — AI management system (Annex A controls)
iso_42001.scope_note: ISO 42001 certifies an organization's AI management system. ACGS cannot be ISO 42001 certified; these rows identify Annex A controls where ACGS runtime evidence supports an AIMS audit.

requirements.requirement: A.2.2 — AI policy: documented policy for the development or use of AI systems
requirements.limitation: Hash-bound runtime policy bundles evidence enforcement of a policy; the organizational AI policy document itself is operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: A.3.2 — AI roles and responsibilities: roles allocated and separation maintained
requirements.limitation: Proposer/validator separation is machine-enforced per decision; org-level role definitions remain operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: A.6.2.6 — AI system operation and monitoring
requirements.limitation: Runtime produces verifiable operational evidence; dashboards, alerting, and review cadence are operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: A.6.2.8 — AI system recording of event logs
requirements.limitation: Append-only hash-chained JSONL for governed side effects; log storage lifecycle is operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: A.8.2 — system documentation and information for users
requirements.verification_method: documentation review: docs/DECISION_RECEIPT_SPEC.md, docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md, docs/CLAIMS.md (make lint-docs does not cover these files)
requirements.limitation: Documentation covers the governance component; whole-system documentation is the integrator's.

requirements.requirement: A.9.2 — processes for responsible use of AI systems
requirements.limitation: ESCALATE-to-human and non-executable DENY are enforcement primitives inside a responsible-use process the organization must define.

soc2.name: SOC 2 — Trust Services Criteria (2017, with 2022 points of focus)
soc2.scope_note: SOC 2 reports on an organization's controls, audited by a CPA firm. ACGS is not SOC 2 attested; these rows identify criteria where ACGS runtime evidence would support an auditor's testing.

requirements.requirement: CC2.1 — the entity obtains/generates relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control
requirements.limitation: Receipts and the hash chain are audit-quality decision evidence for governed actions only.

requirements.requirement: CC4.1 — ongoing and/or separate evaluations to ascertain whether internal control components are present and functioning
requirements.verification_method: uv run --package gove-zone python -m pytest packages/gove-zone/tests/test_cli.py packages/gove-zone/tests/test_replay.py --import-mode=importlib -q
requirements.limitation: verify_chain / proofpack / replay are point-in-time local evaluations; scheduled evaluation programs are operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: CC5.2 — the entity selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives
requirements.limitation: The receipt gate is a technology control activity; entity-level control selection is organizational.

requirements.requirement: CC6.1 — logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets
requirements.limitation: Access to side effects is receipt-mediated, but actor identity is opaque strings — no IAM/PKI, key custody, or revocation; unsigned mode is the default.

requirements.requirement: CC7.2 — the entity monitors system components for anomalies indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors
requirements.limitation: Tampering is detectable (hash chain breaks, receipt hash mismatch); detection is on-verify, not continuous monitoring.

requirements.requirement: CC7.3 — the entity evaluates security events to determine whether they could or have resulted in a failure to meet objectives
requirements.limitation: DENY/ESCALATE events carry full decision context for evaluation; incident-response process is operator-owned.

requirements.requirement: CC8.1 — the entity authorizes, designs, develops, configures, documents, tests, approves, and implements changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures
requirements.limitation: Policy id+hash binding blocks unauthorized policy substitution at decision time; there is no policy lifecycle/approval registry.

requirements.requirement: PI1.2 — system inputs are processed completely, accurately, and timely as authorized (processing integrity over inputs)
requirements.limitation: Executed arguments must hash-match the authorized set for governed calls; ungoverned inputs are out of scope.
